captions.instagram:
How does a spray bottle work?

One squeeze of your finger makes about 4.6 bar, shuts one tiny ball, opens another and tears a millilitre of water into drops thinner than a hair. Pull the trigger of a spray bottle in slow motion and watch it happen.

→ A trigger sprayer is a tiny hand pump: a piston, a spring, two one-way balls and a nozzle that spins water.
→ A dry pump only moves air, so the first few pulls just draw water up the tube. That is priming.
→ Squeeze: a 3 to 1 lever turns 20 newtons into about 4.6 bar, which shuts the inlet ball and opens the outlet.
→ Let go: the spring lowers the pressure, and the air on the bottle's liquid pushes about 1 mL up the tube.
→ At 4.6 bar water leaves at up to 30 m/s, and a swirl chamber spins it into a thin hollow cone.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/sprayclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a spray bottle work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
One squeeze of your finger makes about 4.6 bar, shuts one tiny ball, opens another and tears a millilitre of water into drops thinner than a hair. Pull the trigger of a spray bottle in slow motion and watch it happen.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/sprayclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/sprayclear

In this video:
• A tiny hand pump on a bottle. A trigger sprayer screws onto a bottle and needs no gas or battery.
• Squeeze, then let go. Squeezing with 20 N on a 3 to 1 lever makes about 4.6 bar, which shuts the inlet ball and opens the outlet.
• From a jet to a mist. Pressure gives up to 30 m/s at the hole.
• How far and how fine. Drag brakes small drops within centimetres, and they can evaporate in seconds, while 1 mm drops from the stream setting fly over 4 metres.
• The cousins. A perfume bulb and an airbrush really use suction, from fast air.
• Use it safely. A disinfectant needs its label's contact time, wet on the surface.
